messages.content: We've now got a partner who can do gold wire bonding - not the stud bumping though.
Does someone know if we can have **core_VDD > IO_VDD** when using the ocd IO?
Aside from the totally fair objection of *"wtf are you doing?"* is there anything that would technically prevent me from doing this, such as a diode between core\_vdd and io\_vdd?
No you can't

(1) There is a parasitic body diode.
(2) level converters are not the same to up convert or down convert ... so that wouldn't work anyway.
Thanks tnt 🫡

I was reading the PDK documentation for our IO cells a few days ago, and they mention we don't have circuit under the pad on the IO cells in order to comply with the restrictions of the 3 metal layer process (gf180mcuA). 
So since we are targeting mcuD does this mean there is an opportunity to shorten the io pads by as much as 75um if they where reworked ? 
> The bond pad is non-CUP due to design manual restriction on 3LM.
Given the trouble with bonding I'm not sure I would go to CUP ...
Did this get ported to GF180?
@Archit3ch :  No, that did not get ported to GF180.  The Chipalooza challenge is a step in that direction.
Started a thread.
I have a few ideas... Not at that scale and not with real Xyce models though.

Great. 

Let's chat later starting in like 2 hours from now, or up to a couple hours later than that?
CUP isn't allowed for wedge bonds iirc even at more layers.
I'm travelling without a laptop. Currently on the metro. I can share a 1000-foot plan. 🪽

@Tholin Check out your WSLG design in high resolution: https://infosec.exchange/@infosecdj/117213266219165204

Dmitry is working through the dies I sent him, more to follow soon 🤞

messages.content:
I made this with the new GPT-6 Astra in 20 minutes
Haven't tested it thoroughly, but just did it as a test
I’m gonna assume the default COB PCB is the same as last time. I did not customize the padring this time.

I’m fairly certain pinout won’t change for 1x1. Finer details like number of layers and position of vias might.

Pinout for 1x0p5 might change slightly as the ordering of 4 pins is reversed compared to the die which is likely a recipe for confusion in future

I don’t think 0p5x1 would change, but the run 1 ones aren’t tested yet.

For quarter slot there was talk of using a different connector (fewer pins = cheaper)
I have no idea what the package was that I gave you 😛
These are super cool!
I would love to host a copy on https://data.wafer.space
@InfoSecDJ - Could you do an entire wafer? 😛
Most probably not :D That said, it'd be interesting to have a look at test tiles and features in scribe lanes that got cut
I'll give you all the links when I am done with the whole run, feel free to host a copy there

I'd assume a mere full reticle would be most of the interesting content? 
Unless someone considers the edge partials particularly interesting.
How about the original masks?
I could give it a try, though the resolution/magnification will be very low due to the area that needs to be covered. One 1x1 die takes about ~16h to image
Masks are 4x larger ?  So 10x magnification of mask is the same as 40x of the die.
But yeah still ... full mask is ~ 40x the area of a chip and then there is like ... 25 of them or so ? That's 1.8 year worth 😅
The tyranny of numbers :D
@InfoSecDJ - I think we worked out that my automated microscope (a Labsmore thing from @digshadow)  at PS1 would take roughly like 17 hours to do a mask, which is like one a day.
@carlfk and @Andrew Wingate started doing some stuff which got uploaded at https://data.wafer.space/jaguar-ps1/pyuscope/data/scan/
All depends on the quality+resolution you want to get :)
Always more! 😛
